record.paper_title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems
record.original_question: Suppose A is an F-algebra with continuous inversion on its group G(A) of invertible elements. Must A have no proper topologically invertible elements, where an element x is topologically invertible if there exists a net (z_α) in A with z_α x converging to the identity e, and where a proper topologically invertible element means an element of G^t(A) that is not actually invertible?

evidence.quote: We say that an element x in A is topologically invertible if there is a net (zα) ⊂ A such that limα zα x = e.

The set (group) of all invertible elements of A will be denoted by G(A) and the set of topologically invertible elements – by Gt(A). In general, it is only a multiplicative semigroup and it contains G(A). The proper topologically invertible elements are defined as elements of Gt(A) \ G(A).
Problem 5. Suppose that an F-algebra has a continuous inverse. Does it follow that is has no proper topologically invertible elements ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $A$ be an $F$-algebra, that is, a complete metrizable topological algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ whose topology is given by a translation-invariant metric and whose multiplication is jointly continuous, with unit $e$. Let $G(A)$ denote the (multiplicative) group of invertible elements of $A$. An element $x \in A$ is called topologically invertible if there exists a net $(z_\alpha) \subset A$ such that $\lim_\alpha z_\alpha x = e$; let $G^t(A)$ denote the set of all such elements, which is a multiplicative semigroup containing $G(A)$. An element of $G^t(A) \setminus G(A)$ is called a proper topologically invertible element. Assume further that the inversion map $x \mapsto x^{-1}$ is continuous on $G(A)$. Does it follow that $G^t(A) = G(A)$, i.e., that $A$ has no proper topologically invertible elements?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on dense ideals in topological algebras. Related work studies relationships between topologically invertible elements, topological zero divisors and invertibility in locally convex / locally pseudoconvex algebras, but no source found in the search resolves this specific implication for general F-algebras with continuous inversion.

status_evidence.title: On the topologically invertible elements of a topological algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relations between topologically invertible elements, topological divisors of zero and invertible elements of complete locally convex or locally pseudoconvex unital algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The topic is actively studied but the specific implication under continuous inversion is not resolved in the located sources.

status_evidence.title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems (zbMATH 7084906)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists problems on F-algebras including whether continuous inversion implies absence of proper topologically invertible elements.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recorded as an open problem.
